papers.title: CONCEPTUAL EMERGENCE & GENERATIVE INTELLIGENCE AT THE LIMIT Living Concept Civilization — Flagship Research Monograph 06 STARLI / White Rainbow Civilization · October 2026 ABSTRACT When do interactions among concepts, models, tools and people produce a genuinely new, independently verifiable capacity rather than a novel label or a misleading evaluation threshold? This English-language research monograph develops a falsifiable program for conceptual emergence and generative intelligence. Its research three-coupling is Interaction Generation × New-Function Identification × Counterfactual Verification. The proposed emergence expression compares held-out capability improvement with the strongest viable baseline and a contamination penalty, with all terms requiring operational definition and appropriate normalization before use. RESEARCH DESIGN The volume studies both smooth scaling and possible discontinuities, evaluation-metric sensitivity, training-data leakage, compositional generalization, simple-rule baselines, factorial component ablation, multi-agent collaboration, correlated errors, human-AI complementarity, multimodal grounding, causal interventions, tool-dependence, calibration, cross-model reproducibility, governance, and intergenerational handoff. A claimed capability must survive preregistered unseen tasks, strong comparators, counterfactual perturbations and independent reproduction. A fluent explanation, a generated new term or a model's assertion of consciousness is not evidence of functional emergence. MONOGRAPH STRUCTURE The 82 research chapters each present one distinct proposed chapter-wide operational equation, followed by twelve independently paginated study sections. Thirty advanced physics derivation routes appear in the preface with three-dimensional conceptual diagrams; they are existing physics statements within specified domains and do not establish laws of language or awareness. The concluding 200 Research Gates and 33 Phoenix Answer Embryos each feature one of 233 distinct physical equation anchors. These equations are methodological contrasts and educational prompts, not proof of the emergence hypotheses. A separate Excel workbook indexes chapters, sections, gates, candidate mechanisms and physics anchors. EVIDENCE AND ETHICS This monograph is a theoretical and experimental research agenda. It reports no new trials, controlled effects or validated discoveries; all proposed mechanisms, metrics, forecasts and outcomes are UNVERIFIED until independently tested. The distinction between appearance under a chosen test and a robust new function must be maintained. Consent, intellectual provenance, lawful data use, security and affected persons' right to refuse are hard constraints rather than offsettable penalties. OPEN RESEARCH INVITATION Research Gates reserve space for questions that can be rejected, refined or answered by future researchers. Phoenix Answer Embryos are provisional designs that can be falsified, decomposed, recombined or responsibly retired. The goal is not a permanent claim that machines awaken or that thought obeys physical equations; it is an enduring, contestable toolkit for recognizing and scrutinizing useful new functions. papers.title: STIGMERGIC SWARM MANUFACTURING UNDER QUANTUM MEASUREMENT UNCERTAINTY AT THE LIMIT A Research Architecture for Local Trace Coordination, Uncertainty-Aware Manufacturing, Reference Integrity, and Recoverable Collective Control
papers.summary: STIGMERGIC SWARM MANUFACTURING UNDER QUANTUM MEASUREMENT UNCERTAINTY AT THE LIMIT A Research Architecture for Local Trace Coordination, Uncertainty-Aware Manufacturing, Reference Integrity, and Recoverable Collective Control Research Series: Nano–Quantum Tri-Coupling — Flagship 08Author / Research Imprint: Feng Cheng-en (33) × StarliEdition: English Exploratory Research Monograph, v1.0 (2026) OVERVIEW Stigmergic coordination enables decentralized agents to organize work through marks left in a shared environment. In manufacturing, these marks may designate reserved workspaces, completed operations, defects, material scarcity, assembly dependencies, inspection requirements, or unresolved quality questions. This volume develops an exploratory architecture for investigating that failure mechanism. papers.title: Associative Memory and Cumulative Learning in Artificial Intelligence
papers.summary: Conceptual research paper — not peer reviewed. Persistent artificial intelligence should be evaluated by how accumulated experience changes later judgment. This paper develops that proposition through a critical synthesis of associative memory, evolving agent memory, feedback-based adaptation, and emotional context. The central proposal is to retrieve linked histories of experiences, claims, corrections, and consequences while preserving the distinction between personal significance and evidential reliability. Established research already addresses each major component, so the paper claims neither discovery of associative memory nor a demonstrated replacement for existing architectures. It specifies a candidate retrieval policy and a comparative pilot that could determine whether the proposed integration adds value beyond similarity retrieval and temporal memory. The pilot isolates correction handling, retrieval from indirect cues, resistance to unsupported updates, and contextually appropriate responses. No implementation, experimental results, or superiority claims are reported. The scientific contribution offered here is a reasoned synthesis, an explicit design specification, and a falsifiable evaluation plan whose architectural novelty remains subject to further review. AI assistance was used for literature discovery, development of the proposed specification and evaluation

papers.title: A Survey-Informed Vision of Open-Source Agents: From Rights to Handoffable Maintenance
papers.summary: Open source gives recipients rights to use, study, modify, and redistribute software, but language-model agents distribute behavior across code, learned parameters, prompts, tools, retrieval, configuration, and runtime state. These mechanisms complicate maintenance in open and proprietary systems alike. Public delivery adds a distinct question: whether recipients obtain enough rights, materials, checks, and modification entry points to exercise maintenance capability and pass it onward. We call this objective handoffable maintenance: a verified maintenance result produced by one recipient becomes a practical starting point from which a subsequent recipient can complete a predefined bounded change. This survey-informed vision separates release-side readiness from demonstrated handoff and organizes prior work through eight maintenance-operation families, artifact roles, preservation relations, evidence, and recipient conditions. It identifies four research pathways: independently usable modification sources; public repair resources derived from restricted failures; propagation of public repairs through customized forks; and recipient-side replacement of propagated unreliable contributions. Each pathway specifies its deliverable, preservation requirements, strong comparisons, and falsifiable prediction. A shared evaluation design distinguishes a full-support reference, independent

papers.title: TrajOnco: a multi-agent framework for temporal reasoning over longitudinal EHR for multi-cancer early detection
papers.summary: Abstract Accurate estimation of cancer risk from longitudinal electronic health records (EHRs) could support earlier detection and improved care, but modeling such complex patient trajectories remains challenging. We present TrajOnco, a training-free, multi-agent large language model (LLM) framework designed for scalable multi-cancer early detection. Using a chain-of-agents architecture with long-term memory, TrajOnco performs temporal reasoning over sequential clinical events to generate patient-level summaries, evidence-linked rationales, and predicted risk scores. We evaluated TrajOnco on de-identified Truveta EHR data across 15 cancer types using matched case-control cohorts, predicting risk of cancer diagnosis at 1 year. In zero-shot evaluation, TrajOnco achieved AUROCs of 0.64–0.80, performing comparably to supervised machine learning in a lung cancer benchmark while demonstrating better temporal reasoning than single-agent LLMs. The multi-agent design also enabled effective temporal reasoning with smaller-capacity models such as GPT-4.1-mini. The groundedness of TrajOnco’s output was supported by human evaluation. Furthermore, TrajOnco’s interpretable reasoning outputs can be aggregated to reveal population-level risk patterns that align with established clinical knowledge. Agent Foundry: A Boundary-Preserving Architecture for Governed Agentic Platforms
papers.summary: Agent frameworks expose tools, delegation, memory and human approval, yet the controls attached to a request (identity, tenant, scopes, budgets, deadlines, rate limits, fail behavior) are routinely lost at execution boundaries: delegation, threads, streaming, resume, caching, retrieval and adapter exports. We present Agent Foundry, an open-source Python platform whose architecture is organized around one principle: every control is a property of the request’s execution scope, not an argument that each layer must remember to pass. We formalize this as the Governed Execution Contract (GEC), a meet-semilattice of control scopes with seven invariants, and prove that delegation can only attenuate authority, that deny rules can only tighten resolution, that per-principal rate limits are exact under arbi-trary thread interleavings, that every call yields exactly one audited decision even when the policy source is unreachable, and that admission partitions by principal without cross-shard coordination. On AgentGovBench, a public 48-scenario gov-ernance benchmark, Agent Foundry passes 48/48 in 10 of 10 repetitions, against 46/48 for the best published governed configuration and 13/48 for each of 7 pub-lished framework-native runners; run through the same harness, Microsoft’s Agent Governance Toolkit scores at most 46/48 and Bounded Agents 36/48, and on a 24-scenario suite authored blind

papers.title: A Remotely Delivered Exercise-Based Rehabilitation Program for Patients with Persistent Chemotherapy-Induced Peripheral Neuropathy (EX-CIPN): A Phase I Feasibility Trial
papers.summary: Background: Chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy (CIPN) affects two-thirds of patients who receive neurotoxic chemotherapy. In almost half of these patients, CIPN is persistent, with limited treatment options. Exercise-based rehabilitation shows promising results in improving CIPN-related outcomes, but high-quality research is needed with CIPN symptoms and disability as primary endpoints. Methods: We conducted a phase I single-arm, multi-method pilot study of a 10-week remotely delivered exercise-based rehabilitation program (EX-CIPN) for adult (≥18-years) cancer survivors experiencing CIPN symptoms ≥6 months post-chemotherapy. Primary outcomes were feasibility (accrual, retention, and adherence), acceptability (interviews and surveys), and safety (CTCAE v5). Secondary outcomes included pain, CIPN symptoms, CIPN-related disability, and physiologic assessments. Assessments were conducted at baseline (T1), post-program (T2), and 3 months post-program (T3). Post-program feedback surveys were completed at T2 and semi-structured qualitative video interviews were completed between T2 and T3. Results: In total, 36 participants (median age: 59, 83% female) consented to participate in the study. T1 retention rate (90%), adherence rates (77–96%), and no reported serious adverse events (Grade 3 CTCAE v5) supported study feasibility and safety. Interviews and surveys supported interv

papers.title: Mapping the research landscape of UAV- and eVTOL-enabled emergency medical services: a bibliometric analysis, scoping review, and policy tool assessment
papers.summary: Background Electric vertical takeoff and landing (eVTOL) aircraft and unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) are increasingly recognized as transformative technologies for emergency medical services (EMS). Despite a growing body of evidence on drone-delivered automated external defibrillators (AEDs), blood product logistics, and eVTOL air ambulance simulations, no study has comprehensively mapped this interdisciplinary research landscape while simultaneously analyzing the policy frameworks that govern its implementation. Methods We conducted a triple-method study integrating bibliometric analysis, a scoping review following PRISMA-ScR guidelines, and quantitative policy text analysis. Bibliometric mapping covered 2015 to 2026. The scoping review followed the Joanna Briggs Institute methodology with the PAGER (Patterns, Advances, Gaps, Evidence, Recommendations) synthesis framework, including 168 studies. Policy analysis applied the Rothwell and Zegveld policy tool classification and the Policy Modeling Consistency (PMC) Index to 62 Chinese policy documents related to low-altitude economy and emergency medical rescue (2020–2025), yielding 526 codable policy provisions. Results The bibliometric analysis identified 683 publications across five thematic clusters, with exponential growth from 2022 onward. The scoping review of 168 studies synthesized evidence showing drone-delivered AEDs a

papers.title: Agentic Displacement in Second Language Writing: The Acquisitional Consequences of Delegating Writing to Autonomous AI Browsers
papers.summary: Autonomous AI browsers such as Perplexity Comet and Copilot Mode in Microsoft Edge can receive a writing assignment, draft a response, and submit it with little language produced by the learner. To explain what this means for second language (L2) writing, this conceptual paper introduces the term agentic displacement. Full delegation transfers planning, writing, and revision to the agent, removing opportunities for the learner to produce language and regulate the writing process. The paper argues that this loss may limit language development. Delegation is a continuum; the paper traces its extreme, full replacement, through production-based accounts of acquisition. No empirical data are reported; the paper offers a framework, five testable propositions, and three dimensions of teacher practice: recognizing displacement, auditing tasks for delegability, and using pedagogical judgment to recover the learning a task was meant to produce. The central risk is developmental, not only ethical or procedural.

papers.title: The Reflection Penalty: when managers accept leadership coaching from a human but not an AI agent
papers.summary: Leadership coaching develops managers but is expensive and difficult to scale. AI may be able to help scale access, but “answering machine” like AI coaching agents invite cognitive offloading and weaken learning. We instantiated a human coaching protocol, supported across prior cycles, as a text-based AI coach built to prompt reflective questioning. In the fourth cycle of a design-based research program at a global consulting firm, eight managers received the same protocol from a human coach and the AI coach, applied each session in an observed onboarding activity, and reflected on both in interviews. All eight welcomed the probing questions and preferred the human coach. Notably, they resisted the same protocol of questioning from the AI coach and wanted answers from it instead. This study’s theoretical contribution is the Reflection Penalty, the cost an AI coach pays for asking a user to do the reflective work that makes human coaching effective. Its practical contribution is a jobs-to-be-done map for AI coaching, assembled from proposals participants raised on their own. It divides coaching into distinct jobs and assigns each to the human or the AI best suited to it. Both contributions are offered to those designing AI tools that aim to support reflection

papers.title: Agency and Embodiment Provide Dissociable Benefits to Perception, Metacognition and Neural Processing During Active Sensing
papers.summary: Metacognition, judging how reliable our own perceptual decisions are, is central to adaptive behavior. Such judgments hinge on the reliability of the sensory evidence on which that decision is based, and active sensing through self-directed exploration is known to improve perception itself. Yet, how agency, the authorship over self-initiated actions, and the processing of the sensory consequences, which is implicit to active sensing, modulate metacognition and its calibration, remains unknown. Whether physical embodiment adds to this beyond virtual exploration is similarly unclear, yet relevant both for daily life and for self-monitoring in agentic AI. Here, we combined a naturalistic auditory search paradigm with mobile electroencephalography. Twenty participants performed a target-detection task under three conditions: active embodied exploration , active screen-based exploration, and passive listening to replays of their own trials, while we obtained steady-state auditory evoked potentials (SSAEPs) to characterize stimulus-locked neural responses. We find that both agency conditions improved accuracy, metacognitive sensitivity, and overall SSAEP amplitude relative to passive listening, indicating that agency, rather than whole-body movement, drives these enhancements. papers.title: Anti-CD38 monoclonal antibodies in kidney disease: mechanistic rationale and emerging clinical evidence
papers.summary: Abstract Over the past decades, the therapeutic landscape of nephrology has been transformed by the expanding use of immunosuppressive therapies, reflecting major advances in our understanding of the roles of the innate and adaptive immune systems in the pathogenesis of kidney diseases. While B-cell depletion via rituximab or obinutuzumab has improved immune-mediated kidney disease management, these agents remain insufficient. They spare long-lived plasma cells, memory B cells, and innate effectors, permitting persistent antibody production and ongoing tissue injury. Consequently, increasing attention has focused on anti-CD38 monoclonal antibodies, including daratumumab, isatuximab, and felzartamab, which target several of these pathogenic immune cell populations. Early clinical experience and emerging trial data in diseases such as IgA nephropathy, primary membranous nephropathy, and, most notably, kidney transplantation have suggested potential benefits in selected settings, further supporting their potential role in nephrology. In this narrative review, we summarize the current understanding of the pathophysiological role of CD38-expressing immune cells in kidney diseases and critically evaluate the available clinical evidence on the use of anti-CD38 monoclonal antibody therapies across a spectrum of renal disorders. The review also compares the roles of anti-CD38 monoclonal

papers.title: Digital-Twin-Driven Predictive Maintenance and Fault-Tolerant Control for Electrified Agricultural Machinery: A Multiphysics and Deep Reinforcement Learning Framework for PMSM In-Wheel Drives
papers.summary: Electrified agricultural machinery increasingly relies on permanent-magnet synchronous motor drives that must remain dependable under variable traction, terrain-induced vibration, thermal cycling, contamination, and intermittent duty. Existing work offers mature methods for motor fault diagnosis, digital twins, predictive maintenance, and distributed-drive fault-tolerant control, but their health information is often not shared across diagnosis, maintenance, and control. This article develops a multiphysics digital-twin framework in which electrical, thermal, mechanical, and vibrational evidence maintains a probabilistic health belief that constrains both supervisory maintenance decisions and torque redistribution. The framework formalizes observability, uncertainty-aware health factors, deterministic safety shielding, multi-rate fallback logic, and agriculture-specific traction constraints. Reproducible low-fidelity numerical studies provide preliminary support for context-conditioned residual diagnosis and the revised thermal-continuity trade-off underlying health-aware derating, including robustness and sensitivity analyses. They do not validate sim-to-real transfer or the reinforcement-learning policy itself; those hypotheses remain open for dynamometer and hardware-in-the-loop testing. The results are therefore interpreted as mechanism-level evidence rather than field-perf

papers.title: Exploring or Exploiting Generative AI? A Dual-Path, Dual-Horizon Theory of Employee Incremental and Radical Creativity
papers.summary: Recent research has established that generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is not a unitary workplace resource: exploratory and exploitative use orientations are associated with different forms of employee creativity, and their value depends on employees' capacity to integrate generated knowledge. This article therefore does not present the basic dual path as a new discovery. Instead, it develops a theoretical integration and dynamic extension that asks why the established paths operate differently, when employees should switch between them, and how short-run augmentation can evolve into either capability accumulation or capability substitution. We distinguish expansive and consolidative modes of knowledge integration, theorize phase-congruent switching rather than static ``high-high'' ambidexterity, and position metacognition as a control mechanism that governs both immediate knowledge conversion and longer-run cognitive development. We further specify cultural tightness and psychological safety as directional boundary conditions and distinguish individual creative gains from collective idea-space diversity. The framework converts emerging empirical regularities into falsifiable propositions about task phase, context, and time, providing a research agenda for sustainable human--AI creativity.

papers.title: Polling Without People: Can Silicon Samples of CASM-Inspired LLM Personae Mimic Human Respondents in Pre-Election Polling?

papers.title: Marketing misinformation in the age of AI
papers.summary: Abstract We shine a spotlight on marketing misinformation—claims about products and brands that contradict or distort verifiable facts. Misinformation may be created unintentionally or intentionally by companies, competitors, customers, or third parties seeking to harm companies or consumers. We focus on the role of AI in creating, obfuscating, and disseminating misinformation in the form of text, audio, images, and videos generated using large language models. This type of information can pose a substantial risk for brand safety. Consumers may be aware that AI can generate misinformation but may lack the ability to guard against it. We discuss how different stakeholders in the information ecosystem can help in the prevention and correction of misinformation and propose a future research agenda in this critical and fast‐growing area.

papers.title: Executive Sensemaking of Generative AI Adoption at Enterprise Scale: A Reflexive Thematic Analysis of Cross-Industry Executive Perspectives
papers.summary: This qualitative study examines how senior executives from technology, financial services, and consumer goods publicly make sense of enterprise-scale generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) adoption. Using a purposively selected, bounded single-case design, it applies reflexive thematic analysis to the complete transcript of one moderated industry panel. Three research questions ask: (1) how leaders describe adoption trajectories, maturity, and organizational arrangements; (2) how they reconcile regulation with creative, operational, and governance innovation; and (3) how they frame workforce roles, emerging competencies, and human oversight. Technology–organization–environment, diffusion-of-innovation, and organizational sensemaking perspectives inform interpretation. Nine themes were developed: production-grade diffusion; regulation as creative discipline; industrialized versus distinctive content; personalization and data trust; practitioner-led implementation; divergent workforce responses; critical-thinking demands; human-in-the-loop brand safety; and a shift toward generative engine optimization. Timestamped excerpts and explicit code-to-theme and theme-to-question mappings substantiate the analysis. These findings describe public executive narratives, not independently verified organizational outcomes. A single public transcript and single-analyst interpretation limit

papers.title: Bridging potential and achievement: the AI-enhanced Latin American model of talent development
papers.summary: The persistent gap between individual potential and realized achievement remains a central challenge in gifted education and talent development, particularly when strengths are unrecognized or opportunities are constrained. This Hypothesis and Theory article introduces the AI-Enhanced Latin American Model of Talent Development (AI-LAMTD), an ecological and equity-centered framework that examines underachievement through dynamic potential-opportunity mismatch. Potential is a provisional inference about further domain development under specified conditions; giftedness or high ability describes unusually advanced capacity relative to an explicit reference context; competence comprises acquired domain knowledge and skills; talent is outstanding developed domain competence; and achievement is an observable accomplishment at a particular time. These constructs serve different explanatory and measurement roles. The framework retains four interacting ecological levels—individual development, learning contexts, family and community, and policy and infrastructure—within the cross-cutting principles of equity and capability expansion and cultural relevance and inclusion. Five developmental functions organize possible AI support: recognition of emerging potential, opportunity design, engagement and feedback, developmental monitoring, and support for well-being and flourishing. papers.title: A human-centred, explainable digital system to support emotional self-regulation and everyday psychological well-being
papers.summary: Abstract Self-regulating emotions, thoughts, and behaviours is central to psychological well-being but often difficult to sustain without structured support, particularly under stress or cognitive overload. This study introduces a human-centred digital system designed to support everyday emotional self-regulation through personalised, explainable self-care guidance grounded in established models of emotion regulation and self-regulated behaviour. The system adapts to users’ reported emotional state, cognitive load, time and energy constraints, and personal preferences to generate actionable self-care plans accompanied by natural-language explanations that clarify the system’s reasoning and contrast alternative strategies, supporting user understanding and autonomy. The system is intended for non-clinical, self-care contexts and does not provide diagnosis or treatment. A formative scenario-based evaluation was conducted using three representative non-clinical user archetypes. The generated outputs were independently assessed using a structured rubric, producing mean scenario scores of 4.2–4.8 out of 5. Findings suggest that explainable digital systems can function as cognitive and emotional scaffolding, enhancing reflective engagement and supporting behaviour change in everyday contexts. This work contributes to research at the intersection of behavioural science and technology

papers.title: A scoping review of trust in firsthand and secondhand communication involving humans and artificial intelligence
papers.summary: Conversational and generative artificial intelligence (AI) systems increasingly create and pass information between people. This can make it hard to see who created a claim, whether it was changed, and whom to trust. Many studies examine firsthand human-human and human-AI communication, but less is known about secondhand communication, in which AI or another actor passes on a claim made elsewhere. In these cases, a human decision maker must evaluate the claim and the people or systems that created or passed it on. We present a scoping review built around six minimal motifs that represent firsthand or secondhand communication routes. Humans or AI systems may serve as the source or intermediary, while the decision maker remains human. We screened 3810 records and coded 124 studies to identify 21 trust factors in four dimensions: Decision Maker, Messenger, Message Property, and Environment. Qualitative synthesis also identified four recurring route-level patterns: distorted trust calibration, trust transfer, extremity amplification, and accountability diffusion. These patterns guide future research on AI-mediated communication. Overall, this review provides shared terms and a route-based framework for studying trust in multi-party human-AI communication and designing AI-mediated communication systems.

papers.title: Video and digital games: Historical controversies, benefits, and risks for children and adolescents
papers.summary: Video and digital games have been the focus of sustained public and scientific debate since their commercial emergence in the late 1970s, particularly regarding their effects on children and adolescents. Early public and scientific discourse frequently portrayed gaming as a source of physical injury, addiction, aggression, social isolation, academic problems, and moral decline. However, subsequent empirical research has produced a substantially more differentiated picture of both the benefits and risks of gaming. This review examines the historical foundations of controversies surrounding video and digital games and synthesizes contemporary evidence concerning their cognitive, emotional, social, therapeutic, and physical effects. . Research indicates that moderate, purposeful gaming may improve visuospatial abilities, attentional control, problem-solving, mood regulation, social connection, and selected educational outcomes. Gaming-based interventions have also demonstrated therapeutic potential, particularly for depressive symptoms and attention-related difficulties among young people. At the same time, important risks remain, especially when gaming becomes excessive, compulsive, or disruptive to everyday functioning. These include repetitive-strain injuries, sleep disruption, problematic gaming, and adverse mental-health and academic outcomes. Evidence concerning violent game

papers.title: AI-Driven Smart Irrigation System Using Edge-Based Embedded Controllers
papers.summary: This study brings out a new AI-based smart irrigation device aimed at solving the increasing problem of water shortage and poor agricultural procedures using emulated edge-based controllers. This combination of environmental sensing, lightweight machine learning algorithms and actuation on microcontrollers enables the system to do real time, adaptive irrigation scheduling. Their implementation of important parts like Raspberry Pi 4 as an AI inference module and an STM32 microcontroller as an actuator controller accelerates the responsiveness, increases security, and saves energy consumption since there is no need in cloud computing. Using the local climatic and soil moisture data the machine learning model identifies optimum irrigation time and duration looking at various parameters such as temperature, humidity, rain and crop-specific thresholds. The whole decision-making process is automated and carried out at the edge that makes it functional even without interruption in areas with poor or no internet connection. This was done by conducting extensive field tests within the semi-arid agricultural areas to prove the efficacy of the recommended solution. The findings show that there is a considerable gain in the efficiency of resources, with up to 38 percent of reduction of water use and 20 percent of increase in the yield of the crops contrasted to the conventional time-based

papers.title: STRATEGIC HUMAN RESOURCE MANAGEMENT, DIGITAL COMMERCE, AND AI-DRIVEN MARKETING: AN INTEGRATED FRAMEWORK FOR SUSTAINABLE BUSINESS GROWTH AND ORGANIZATIONAL PERFORMANCE
papers.summary: Digital transformation has intensified the need for organizations to align workforce strategy, digital commerce systems, and intelligent marketing capabilities. This comprehensive review examines how strategic human resource management, digital commerce, and AI-driven marketing support sustainable business growth and organizational performance. The review synthesizes literature on digital workforce planning, reskilling, platform-based commerce, marketing automation, predictive analytics, customer personalization, employee engagement, organizational resilience, and ethical governance. The findings indicate that strategic human resource management provides the capability foundation by developing digital skills, adaptive leadership, cross-functional collaboration, and continuous learning. Digital commerce serves as the value-creation and delivery infrastructure through online platforms, fintech integration, omnichannel systems, and network-based business models. AI-driven marketing serves as the customer-intelligence mechanism by enabling segmentation, forecasting, automation, personalization, and real-time engagement. Their coordinated integration can strengthen innovation, productivity, customer experience, revenue generation, and resilience. However, sustainable outcomes depend on reliable data, employee trust, human oversight, privacy protection, algorithmic fairness, and acco

papers.title: Oxygen deficiency and valency reconstruction in multiferroic V-doped HfO 2
papers.summary: The interplay of oxygen deficiency and vanadium multiple valency in the candidate multiferroic V-doped P c a 2 1 hafnia HfO 2 is studied by first-principles calculations. Low-lying V majority gap states accept electrons from oxygen-vacancy donors, reducing their formation energy, and converting nominal V 4 + centers into V 3 + . The resulting local magnetization and screening changes are reflected in the calculated V core-level shifts, which are consistent with the experimentally observed x-ray photoelectron spectroscopy signatures. The calculated V 3 + / V 4 + population ratio determined by oxygen vacancies only matches experiment in reducing conditions, suggesting that additional electron reservoirs may contribute under atomic-layer-deposition growth conditions. A similar scenario also seems to apply to the recently observed multiferroicity in Cr-doped hafnia, where oxygen deficiency is expected from the synthesis route.

papers.title: Atropine-Associated Central Anticholinergic Syndrome during Carotid Artery Stenting: A Case Report
papers.summary: Acute neurobehavioral deterioration during carotid artery stenting (CAS) requires prompt evaluation for serious neurological complications. We report a patient in their 70s who developed profound hyperactive delirium approximately 15 minutes after receiving prophylactic intravenous atropine (0.25 mg) during CAS. The episode was characterized by severe agitation, bilateral mydriasis, and facial flushing without focal neurological deficits. Repeated angiography and subsequent neuroimaging showed no evidence of thromboembolism, intracranial hemorrhage, cerebral edema, or cerebral hyperperfusion. Contrast-induced encephalopathy and cerebral hyperperfusion syndrome were considered but were less consistent with the overall clinical, temporal, and radiographic findings. The patient returned to neurological and cognitive baseline approximately 16 hours after symptom onset without specific antidotal treatment. The close temporal relationship to atropine exposure and characteristic neurobehavioral and autonomic features favored atropine-associated central anticholinergic syndrome, which should be considered in the differential diagnosis of acute neurobehavioral deterioration during CAS.

papers.title: Case Report: Four-year durable remission, cerebral oligoprogression, and femoral head necrosis following severe recurrent immune checkpoint inhibitor-related pneumonitis in a patient with stage IV lung adenocarcinoma
papers.summary: Severe immune checkpoint inhibitor-related pneumonitis (CIP) typically leads to the permanent discontinuation of immunotherapy; however, its long-term oncological outcomes and late drug toxicity remain poorly defined. This report describes a patient with stage IV lung adenocarcinoma who, following recurrent grade 3 CIP, achieved durable systemic remission for more than 4 years and displayed a distinctive pattern of cerebral oligoprogression. A 66-year-old male patient with stage IV lung adenocarcinoma achieved a partial response (PR) after four cycles of sintilimab combined with chemotherapy. Three weeks after the last dose, he developed grade 3 CIP complicated by acute pulmonary embolism. Recurrence occurred twice because of overly rapid corticosteroid tapering and was ultimately controlled through an ultralow tapering regimen (50 mg/day prednisone initially, reduced by 5 mg per week) combined with pirfenidone for antifibrotic therapy. Following the resolution of CIP, no further systemic antitumor therapy was administered. During 48 months of follow-up, the patient maintained complete remission (CR) of extracranial metastases; the sole site of progression was a solitary cerebellar lesion, which exhibited three episodes of oligoprogression, each of which was successfully managed with either radiotherapy or bevacizumab-based therapy. papers.title: Artificial Intelligence Related Sentiments and Perceptions on Federated Social Networks: A Computational Text Analysis
papers.summary: This study aims to examine public perceptions of artificial intelligence (AI) on federated social networks, specifically Bluesky and Mastodon. While existing research focuses on centralized platforms, a significant gap exists regarding AI perception within decentralized networks. This study addresses this gap through computational analysis of AI related posts in Bluesky and Mastodon. A text-as-data approach was employed to analyze 61,285 posts collected from Bluesky and Mastodon between January 1, 2023, and January 1, 2025. The methodology integrated topic modeling, sentiment analysis, and text analysis to identify prevalent themes, sentiment polarity, and discussion patterns within AI-related discourse. Findings demonstrate predominantly positive sentiment towards AI across both platforms, with trust, anticipation, and joy as primary emotional responses, accompanied by underlying fear and anxiety. Platform-specific variations emerged: Mastodon discourse centers on creativity, digital art, and societal-ethical implications including regulation, bias, and disinformation concerns. Conversely, Bluesky posts emphasize economic and geopolitical dimensions, featuring startups, funding, stock markets, and international policy. papers.title: Responsible integration of generative AI and LLMs in higher education: Empirical insights and a framework for teaching and learning
papers.summary: Generative AI (GenAI) tools are rapidly reshaping university learning environments, yet pedagogical and ethical frameworks have not developed at the same pace as their adoption. Adopting a multidisciplinary approach, this study combines empirical evidence from a survey of 117 undergraduate Engineering and Health Sciences students with the pedagogical perspectives of university lecturers. It examines how students currently use GenAI and how these tools can be meaningfully integrated into teaching and learning. Findings show that students’ first exposure to GenAI is mainly driven by informal social media channels rather than institutional guidance, resulting in uneven and often unguided adoption. The study also identifies a “contradictory profile” in 11% of the sample: students who perceive GenAI use as a form of cheating while also expressing a strong demand for formal training on its academic integration. From the lecturers’ perspective, GenAI offers opportunities to support content creation, assessment design, and instructional workflows, provided that human-led teaching remains central. By integrating observed student behaviors with expert recommendations, this research proposes an ethical framework and practical guidelines for the responsible integration of GenAI in higher education. papers.title: Strip flatness prediction in cold rolling: a review of models, challenges, and emerging directions
papers.summary: Abstract Cold rolling is one of the most widely applied metal-forming processes, where strip flatness is a critical quality requirement affecting downstream manufacturability, dimensional accuracy and product performance. Flatness defects arise from non-uniform longitudinal stresses generated through tightly coupled interactions between roll bite mechanics, roll stack deformation, friction and lubrication, material behaviour and post-bite buckling. Although numerous modelling strategies exist, the literature remains fragmented across analytical, numerical, hybrid and data driven approaches, making it difficult to identify the most appropriate tools for prediction and control. This review provides a unified framework for strip flatness prediction in cold rolling, presenting a structured taxonomy of modelling approaches and evaluating their assumptions, predictive capability, computational cost and industrial applicability. Analytical and semi-analytical models are compared with numerical techniques and hybrid coupled formulations. Key transversal components, including constitutive laws, friction and lubrication models and buckling formulations, are examined with respect to their influence on widthwise stress distributions and the formation of flatness defects.
